answers.value: All life new-business applications flagged in the policy administration system (ALIP) as replacing existing coverage; scope is the individual case, covering the applicant and each existing insurer identified on the replacement form.
The statutory notice window for the case: replacement notices must reach the applicant and each existing insurer within 5 business days of application receipt in the current new-business cycle.

The ALIP replacement register shows applicant name, application/policy number, each existing insurer and policy number, notice type, and send date; a case missing an existing-insurer address is held and not bound.
Count of replacement-flagged cases in ALIP equals the count of notices generated and sent (applicant plus each existing insurer); the delta on the daily new-business batch must be 0.

Copies of issued notices and proof of mailing stored in the policy file under /UW/<policyNumber>/replacement/ with send timestamp and version, retained the longer of 5 years or until the next market-conduct exam.

Cases where a notice cannot be issued on time are logged in the GRC platform as a replacement-notice exception, assignee New Business Case Manager, with disposition (expedite / cure / decline-to-bind) and reason.

The notice references the applicable state Life Insurance Replacement Model Regulation (NAIC Model #613) and the carrier's replacement procedure; the citation is printed on the notice and recorded on the case.
Notices and proof of mailing are retained the longer of 5 years or the period to the next state market-conduct examination, per the replacement regulation retention provision.
Applicant and existing-insurer notices are sent within 5 business days of application receipt; the send date is stamped and compared to the statutory deadline on the case checklist.
All replacement-flagged life cases issued in the quarter (100% census), reconciled against the ALIP replacement register.
PASS = 100% of replacement cases have applicant and existing-insurer notices sent within 5 business days with proof of mailing on file; FAIL = any case missing a required notice or sent late.
Late or missing notices escalate to the Compliance Analyst and New Business Case Manager; the case is not bound until cured and a corrective note is filed in GRC.
Acceptance = both notices issued within statutory time, correct existing-insurer detail, regulation citation present, and copies retained; recorded on the case checklist.
Issued notices and mailing proof reside in the policy file /UW/<policyNumber>/replacement/ and in the ALIP case notes.

Applicable rule: the state Life Insurance Replacement Model Regulation (NAIC Model #613) replacement-notice and 20-day free-look provisions; notice-timing and retention requirements are cited on the case.

checklist.step: Issue and document the replacement notice within the statutory time
checklist.value: Replacement notices are generated and sent within 5 business days of application receipt, with the send action and timestamp recorded on the ALIP case.

testing.step: Verify notice timeliness on issued cases
testing.value: Sample replacement cases and confirm both notices were sent within 5 business days; 0 late notices tolerated.

checklist.step: Retain the replacement notice and proof of mailing in the policy file
checklist.value: Signed notice copies and mailing proof are filed under /UW/<policyNumber>/replacement/ with version and timestamp.

testing.value: For each sampled case, the policy file contains applicant and existing-insurer notices plus proof of mailing; missing documents fail the review.

answers.value: Every life replacement/suitability determination made by the underwriter, subject to supervisory review before the case proceeds; scope is the individual case's suitability file in ALIP.
The review is performed before binding/issue, within 2 business days of the underwriter's suitability determination.

The suitability worksheet shows customer needs, existing-vs-proposed policy comparison, replacement rationale, and the underwriter's determination; incomplete worksheets are returned to the underwriter.
The number of suitability determinations awaiting review equals the number reviewed and signed; no case advances to issue without a recorded supervisory review.
The supervisory review note (approve/return with reasons) is stored on the case with reviewer, timestamp, and version; retained 5 years.
Determinations judged unsuitable are returned with documented reasons and tracked as a review exception in the GRC platform until resolved.
Monthly sample of at least 10% of reviewed suitability cases, minimum 25 files per month.
PASS = every sampled case has a completed supervisory review with rationale before issue; FAIL = any case issued without review or with an unsupported determination.
Failures escalate to the Compliance Manager; affected cases are re-reviewed and, if already issued, remediated through the free-look/rescission process.
Acceptance = documented supervisory sign-off, a complete suitability worksheet, and a rationale consistent with the recommendation.
Evidence resides in the case suitability file in ALIP and the supervisory review log.

checklist.step: Perform documented peer/supervisory review before issue
checklist.value: A Senior Underwriter reviews the suitability determination and records approve/return with rationale on the case.

testing.value: Sample issued cases and confirm each has a supervisory review recorded before issue; 0 uncontrolled issues.

checklist.step: Sample review completed suitability files monthly
checklist.value: At least 10% of reviewed cases (min 25) are re-examined by underwriting management each month for suitability soundness.

testing.step: Confirm sample size and findings disposition
testing.value: Monthly sample meets the minimum and every finding has a recorded disposition; shortfalls are escalated.

checklist.step: Confirm suitability was assessed against customer needs before proceeding
checklist.value: The supervisory review checks that customer needs, existing coverage, and replacement rationale support suitability before the case advances.

testing.value: For sampled cases, a completed needs/suitability assessment supports the determination; 0 cases advance without it.

answers.value: The complete replacement-review documentation set for the case (suitability worksheet, policy comparison, replacement notices, and supervisory sign-off) to be retained for state examination access.
At case close/issue; documentation is retained the longer of 5 years or the period to the next market-conduct examination.
Each retained record carries policy number, applicant, document type, author, date, and retention flag; a document missing its type or date is not accepted into the file.
The count of documents retained per case reconciles to the replacement checklist (worksheet + comparison + notices + sign-off); any missing artifact is logged as a gap.
Documents are stored in OpenText/ALIP under /UW/<policyNumber>/replacement/ with immutable timestamp and version; retention set the longer of 5 years or next exam.
Cases with an incomplete file are flagged in GRC with disposition (locate / re-create / accept-gap with reason), assignee Underwriting Assistant, until the file is complete.
Sampled retained records trace back to their source screens in ALIP and the original notice PDFs; each document opens and matches the case index.
The case status in ALIP is set to 'retained/closed' only after the replacement documentation set is confirmed complete.
Document dates (notice send date, review date, retention start) are populated and consistent with the workflow timeline.
Retention is governed by the state Life Insurance Replacement Model Regulation record-retention provision; the citation is recorded on the retention record.
The file is retained the longer of 5 years or until the next state examination, matching the replacement-regulation requirement.
Not a filing task; the retention deadline (retention start plus required period) is recorded and monitored against the disposal schedule.
Quarterly sample of 25 closed replacement cases checked for a complete and retrievable documentation set.
PASS = 100% of sampled cases have all required documents retained, retrievable, and correctly dated; FAIL = any missing or non-retrievable document.
Incomplete files are escalated to the Compliance Analyst; the document is located or re-created and a GRC exception records the gap and remediation.
Acceptance = complete, indexed, retrievable replacement file with correct retention period applied.
Documents reside in OpenText/ALIP under /UW/<policyNumber>/replacement/ with the retention log entry.

ALIP replacement-register fields (policy number, existing insurer, notice dates, retention flag) are defined in the underwriting data dictionary; the retained-document count reconciles to issued replacement cases.
Applicable rule: the state Life Insurance Replacement Model Regulation (NAIC Model #613) record-retention provision (longer of 5 years or next exam); cited on the retention record.

checklist.step: Assemble and index the complete replacement file
checklist.value: Worksheet, comparison, notices, and sign-off are filed under /UW/<policyNumber>/replacement/ and indexed to the case.

testing.value: Sampled cases return a complete, retrievable file on demand; missing documents fail.

checklist.step: Preserve an immutable audit trail for retained records
checklist.value: Each document carries author, timestamp, and version; edits are versioned rather than overwritten.

testing.value: Sampled records show an unbroken version history with no gaps or overwrites.

answers.value: The replacement rationale for the case, evaluated by comparing existing and proposed policy values and costs; scope is the individual applicant's existing and proposed contracts.
During suitability review of the case, before binding/issue in the current new-business cycle.

The comparison worksheet is populated with existing and proposed premium, cash/surrender value, surrender charge, death benefit, and any new contestability/suicide period; blanks are cured before the rationale is accepted.
In-force values on the worksheet reconcile to the existing insurer's statement and ALIP; the proposed values reconcile to the illustration, with a 0 variance requirement.
The completed comparison and rationale are stored on the case with author, timestamp, and version; retained 5 years.
A rationale that does not support replacement is logged as a suitability exception in GRC and returned to the underwriter with reasons before the case proceeds.
The comparison uses the approved illustration/rating basis (current rating manual version) and in-force figures from the existing insurer's statement of values.
Sensitivity of the recommendation to key assumptions (crediting rate, surrender charges, expense loads) is documented; swings beyond +/-10% of illustrated value trigger re-review.
Materiality is set at a cost/benefit difference of 5% of face or surrender value; differences above it require Senior Underwriter sign-off on the rationale.
Worksheet figures trace to the existing insurer's statement of values and the proposed illustration screen in ALIP.
The suitability status advances to 'rationale reviewed' only after the comparison is complete and consistent.
Effective/valuation dates on the existing and proposed contracts are populated and aligned to the comparison date.
Quarterly sample of 25 replacement cases with a documented rationale and completed comparison.
PASS = the rationale is supported by the value/cost comparison and reconciles to source; FAIL = rationale unsupported or comparison values do not reconcile.
Unsupported rationales are returned to the underwriter and escalated to the Senior Underwriter; the case is not issued until the rationale is corrected or the replacement is withdrawn.
Acceptance = a documented cost/benefit comparison that supports the replacement recommendation and reconciles to source values.
Evidence resides in the case suitability file in ALIP with the comparison worksheet attached.
The comparison uses the approved illustration/rating basis (current rating manual version); in-force parameters are sourced from the existing insurer's statement of values, recorded on the worksheet.
Existing vs proposed fields (premium, cash value, surrender charge, death benefit) are defined per the comparison worksheet; totals reconcile to ALIP and the in-force statement.

checklist.step: Independently review the replacement rationale
checklist.value: The Senior Underwriter re-checks the value/cost comparison and the stated rationale before the case proceeds.

testing.value: Sampled cases show an independent review consistent with the comparison; unsupported rationales are caught.

checklist.step: Document the comparison and rationale in the file
checklist.value: The completed comparison worksheet and written rationale are retained on the case.

testing.value: Each sampled replacement case has a complete comparison and rationale on file; missing documentation fails.

checklist.step: Confirm the replacement is suitable given costs and needs
checklist.value: The rationale review confirms the proposed policy serves the customer's needs after weighing surrender charges, new contestability, and cost differences.

testing.value: For sampled cases, the documented comparison supports a suitable replacement; disadvantageous replacements are declined or escalated.

answers.value: The suitability findings package for the case, routed to Compliance for sign-off before the replacement is finalized; scope is the individual case's suitability determination and supporting comparison.
After supervisory review and before issue, routed within 1 business day so Compliance can sign off inside the case's statutory window.
The routing record carries case number, findings summary, suitability determination, supervisory sign-off, and the compliance queue/assignee; a package missing sign-off is not routed.
The count of cases requiring compliance sign-off equals the count routed and received in the compliance queue; the delta must be 0 at end of day.
The routing action and compliance decision are recorded in the GRC platform and on the ALIP case with timestamp and version; retained 5 years.
Packages returned by Compliance are logged as an exception in GRC with reasons and re-worked; the case is held until sign-off is obtained.
All replacement cases requiring compliance sign-off in the quarter (100% census) checked for a routed package and recorded decision.
PASS = every case is routed to Compliance with a complete package and a recorded sign-off before issue; FAIL = any case issued without compliance sign-off.
Cases returned or not signed off escalate to the Compliance Manager; the case cannot be bound until sign-off is captured or the replacement is withdrawn.
Acceptance = complete findings package routed to Compliance and a recorded sign-off (or documented return) before issue.
Evidence resides in the GRC compliance-review record and the ALIP case workflow history.

checklist.step: Route findings to the next authority level with a recommendation
checklist.value: The suitability findings and a recommendation are routed to Compliance for sign-off, with the referral recorded on the case.

testing.value: Sampled cases show the findings were routed with a recommendation and a recorded compliance decision; 0 unrouted cases.

checklist.step: Document the sign-off in the case file
checklist.value: The compliance decision and rationale are stored on the case in GRC/ALIP.

testing.value: Each sampled case has a retained compliance sign-off before issue; missing sign-off fails.

answers.value: The referred risk assessed against current portfolio strategy and accumulation position; scope is the individual referral plus the relevant line-of-business/geography accumulation view.
During senior/chief underwriter review of the referral, using the current in-force accumulation snapshot.
The alignment record captures the risk's LOB, geography, limit, and how it sits against appetite and current accumulation; an assessment missing the accumulation reference is not accepted.
The exposure figures used reconcile to the portfolio accumulation report from the actuarial/exposure platform; the added limit ties to the referral, with 0 variance.
The alignment assessment and its accumulation basis are recorded on the referral with author, timestamp, and version; retained 5 years.
Risks that breach appetite or accumulation tolerance are logged as an exception requiring CUO approval, with documented reason, before the referral proceeds.
The accumulation position is drawn from the approved production version of the exposure/cat model and the current appetite matrix.
Sensitivity of the accumulation view to added limit and correlation assumptions is documented; a swing beyond +/-10% of the zone aggregate triggers CUO review.
Materiality is set at the appetite/zone-limit threshold; risks that move the aggregate above it require CUO sign-off.
Quarterly sample of 20 referrals with a portfolio-alignment assessment, re-checked against the accumulation report.
PASS = the recorded alignment ties to the accumulation report and respects appetite; FAIL = alignment claim not supported by accumulation data or breaches appetite without CUO approval.
Misaligned risks route to the CUO with documented rationale; the referral is not approved until within appetite or explicitly approved as an exception.
The exposure/cat model version used is the approved production release recorded on the referral.
Parameters (in-force exposures, zone definitions, correlation set) are sourced from the governed accumulation dataset and the appetite matrix.

checklist.step: Assess the risk against documented appetite by LOB, geography, and industry
checklist.value: The alignment check compares the referral to the current appetite matrix for its line, geography, and class.

testing.value: Sampled referrals fall within documented appetite or carry a CUO-approved exception; 0 silent breaches.

checklist.step: Confirm the risk fits target classes and accumulation limits
checklist.value: The risk is checked against defined target classes and current accumulation before alignment is recorded.

testing.value: Sampled alignment records tie to the accumulation report and respect zone limits; breaches are escalated.

answers.value: The approve/modify/decline decision on the referral, recorded with written rationale in the underwriting system; scope is the individual referral under senior/chief underwriter review.
At referral disposition, documented within 24 hours of the review being completed.
The decision record shows the outcome (approve/modify/decline), any conditions, the written rationale, the reviewer, and the authority level; a decision without rationale is rejected.
Every referral in the review queue has exactly one recorded decision; open referrals reconcile to decisions plus pending, with no orphaned or duplicate dispositions.
The decision and rationale are stored on the referral in ALIP with author, timestamp, and version; retained 5 years.
Decisions exceeding the reviewer's authority are logged as an exception and routed to the CUO for approval before they take effect.
Any pricing or model basis cited in the rationale references the approved production rating manual/model version.
Where the decision modifies terms, the sensitivity of the outcome to the changed condition (limit, retention, price) is noted in the rationale.
Materiality is the authority-matrix threshold for the LOB; decisions above it require CUO sign-off recorded on the referral.
The decision, conditions, and rationale are documented on the referral record in ALIP at disposition.
The referring underwriter (and broker where applicable) are recorded as the decision recipients on the referral.
Monthly sample of 25 referral decisions across approve/modify/decline outcomes.
PASS = every sampled decision has written rationale, is within the reviewer's authority (or CUO-approved), and records any conditions; FAIL = missing rationale or out-of-authority decision.
Out-of-authority or unsupported decisions are escalated to the CUO and corrected; the referral disposition is held until compliant.
Referral fields (outcome code, conditions, rationale text, authority level, reviewer) are defined in the underwriting data dictionary.
Decision counts by outcome reconcile to the referral log; the total ties to referrals received minus pending.
The decision is made within the reviewer's authority per the underwriting authority matrix v3.2; any delegation to Senior Underwriter/CUO is documented on the referral.
Any pricing/model basis cited is the approved production version; the parameter source (rating manual, model run) is recorded with the decision rationale.

checklist.step: Document the referral decision within 24 hours
checklist.value: The approve/modify/decline outcome and rationale are recorded on the referral within 24 hours of review completion.

testing.value: Sampled referrals show a documented decision within 24 hours; late or undocumented decisions fail.

checklist.step: Confirm the decision is within authority limits
checklist.value: The reviewer's authority for premium, limit, and LOB is checked before the decision is finalized.

testing.value: Sampled decisions fall within the reviewer's authority or carry CUO approval; 0 out-of-authority bindings.

answers.value: The assumptions stated in the underwriting narrative for the referred risk (exposure basis, loss expectations, pricing and terms rationale); scope is the individual referral's narrative.
During senior/chief underwriter review of the referral, before disposition.
Each challenged assumption is recorded with the original statement, the challenge, and its resolution; a narrative with unchallenged material assumptions is returned for rework.
The exposure and loss figures cited in the narrative reconcile to the rating/model output; discrepancies above tolerance are flagged, targeting 0 unexplained variance.
The challenge log and its resolutions are stored on the referral with author, timestamp, and version; retained 5 years.
Assumptions that cannot be substantiated are logged as an exception and drive a request for additional analysis before the referral proceeds.
Assumptions are challenged against the approved rating basis and the current production model version referenced in the narrative.
Sensitivity of the pricing/terms to each key assumption (rate, frequency, severity, limit) is documented; a swing beyond +/-10% of technical price triggers actuarial review.
Materiality is set at 10% of technical premium or the authority-matrix limit; assumptions moving the case above it require documented substantiation.
Monthly sample of 20 referrals with a documented assumption-challenge log.
PASS = material assumptions are identified, challenged, and resolved with support; FAIL = a material assumption accepted without challenge or substantiation.
Unsubstantiated assumptions route to a request for additional analysis and, where pricing is affected, to the Pricing Actuary before disposition.
Acceptance = a documented challenge log showing each material assumption tested and resolved before the referral is disposed.
Evidence resides on the referral record in ALIP with the challenge log attached.
Assumptions are challenged against the approved rating basis/model version and the stated parameter sources; deviations are noted on the narrative review with the source cited.

checklist.step: Peer-challenge the narrative assumptions
checklist.value: The reviewer challenges each material assumption in the narrative and records the resolution.

testing.value: Sampled referrals show material assumptions were challenged and resolved; unchallenged assumptions fail.

checklist.step: Obtain actuarial input on large or assumption-sensitive accounts
checklist.value: Where pricing assumptions are material, the Pricing Actuary reviews the basis before disposition.

testing.step: Verify actuarial review for qualifying accounts
testing.value: Sampled large/assumption-sensitive referrals evidence actuarial review; missing review fails.

answers.value: The approval decision and any conditions for the referral, communicated to the referring underwriter; scope is the individual referral disposition.
Immediately after disposition, communicated to the referring underwriter within the agreed SLA of 1 business day.
The communication record shows the decision, conditions, referring underwriter, channel, and send timestamp; a referral without a recorded communication is not closed.
The count of disposed referrals equals the count with a communication logged to the referring underwriter; the delta must be 0.
The communication is captured in the ALIP workflow history with timestamp and version; retained 5 years.
Communications missed within the SLA are logged as an exception with reason and re-sent; repeated misses are escalated to the UW Operations Manager.
The decision and conditions communicated are the ones documented on the referral at disposition.
The referring underwriter is the recorded recipient; broker/agent notification, where applicable, is noted separately.
Monthly sample of 25 disposed referrals checked for a timely, complete communication.
PASS = decision and conditions communicated to the referring underwriter within 1 business day and logged; FAIL = late, missing, or incomplete communication.
Missed communications are re-sent and logged as an exception; the referral is not treated as closed until the communication is confirmed.
The delegation matrix (authority matrix v3.2) confirms the communicated decision was made at the correct authority level; recorded on the referral.
Acceptance = decision and conditions communicated to the referring underwriter within the agreed SLA with confirmation logged; evidence in the ALIP workflow history and case notes.

checklist.step: Communicate and document the decision promptly
checklist.value: The decision and conditions are conveyed to the referring underwriter within the SLA and recorded on the referral.

testing.value: Sampled referrals show the decision communicated within 1 business day with a logged confirmation; late communications fail.

checklist.step: Return the decision with recommendation to the referring level
checklist.value: The disposition is routed back to the referring underwriter with conditions and rationale.

testing.value: Sampled referrals evidence a communicated decision back to the originator; open loops fail.

answers.value: The referred risk's risk analysis, pricing rationale, and proposed terms, reviewed independently of the originating underwriter; scope is the individual referral.
During senior/chief underwriter review of the referral, before disposition.
The independent-review record captures the risk analysis, technical price, proposed terms, and the reviewer's concurrence or exceptions; an incomplete package is returned.
The technical price and exposures re-derived in review reconcile to the originating rating/model output; differences above tolerance are documented, targeting 0 unexplained variance.
The independent review, including any re-run figures, is stored on the referral with author, timestamp, and version; retained 5 years.
Pricing or terms that fail the independent check are logged as an exception and returned with recommendations before the referral proceeds.
The review uses the approved production rating manual/model version to re-check the technical price.
Sensitivity of the price/terms to key drivers (rate level, limit, deductible, credits) is documented; swings beyond +/-10% of technical price trigger actuarial concurrence.
Materiality is set at 10% of technical premium or the authority-matrix limit; results above it require CUO sign-off.
Monthly sample of 20 referrals with a documented independent review of risk and pricing.
PASS = independent review re-derives the price within tolerance and confirms terms; FAIL = price/terms not independently supported or variance unexplained.
Failed reviews return to the originator with recommendations and, where pricing is affected, to the Pricing Actuary; disposition is held until resolved.
Acceptance = an independent review that reconciles the technical price and confirms the proposed terms, or documents required changes.
Evidence resides on the referral record in ALIP with the review note and any re-run outputs attached.
The independent review re-checks the approved pricing/model version and parameter sources (rating manual version, mortality/cat model run); the sources are recorded in the review note.

checklist.step: Independently review risk and pricing
checklist.value: A reviewer independent of the originator re-checks the analysis, technical price, and terms.

testing.value: Sampled referrals show an independent review whose price reconciles to source; unreconciled cases fail.

checklist.step: Confirm filed rates and rating factors were applied correctly
checklist.value: The review re-checks that the technical price uses the filed rates and approved rating factors.

testing.value: Sampled referrals price against filed rates; deviations require an authority-matrix exception, else fail.

answers.value: The referred risk checked against applicable treaty terms, form-filing requirements, and regulatory constraints before disposition; scope is the individual referral and its ceded/treaty position.
During senior/chief underwriter review of the referral, before binding, using the treaties and filings in force at the effective date.

The compliance-check record captures the treaty reference and cession fit, the form/rate filing status for the state, and any surplus-lines or regulatory constraint; a missing filing reference blocks binding.
The risk's limit/retention reconciles to the treaty's capacity and attachment; the state and form used tie to the approved filing, with 0 mismatches permitted.
The compliance confirmation and its citations are recorded in the GRC platform and on the referral with timestamp and version; retained 5 years.
Risks outside treaty terms or lacking an approved filing are logged as an exception requiring facultative placement or CUO approval before binding.
Applicable treaty terms, form/rate filing status (SERFF), and surplus-lines/filed-rate requirements are cited on the compliance record.
The compliance confirmation is retained 5 years with the referral to support market-conduct examination.
Where a form/rate filing is a prerequisite, the approved-filing effective date is confirmed to precede the risk's effective date.
Quarterly sample of 25 referrals bound after a treaty/regulatory compliance check.
PASS = the risk fits treaty terms and uses approved forms/filings with constraints satisfied; FAIL = out-of-treaty cession or unfiled form/rate used.
Non-conforming risks route to Reinsurance (facultative) or Compliance and require CUO approval before binding; otherwise the risk is declined.
The treaty period and the approved-filing effective dates in force at the risk's effective date define the in-scope constraints for the check.
Applicable rules: the reinsurance treaty terms, the state form/rate filing (SERFF) status, and surplus-lines/filed-rate requirements; the specific citations are recorded in GRC on the referral.

checklist.step: Confirm current, approved form filings are used
checklist.value: The forms applied to the risk are checked against the approved SERFF filings for the state before binding.

testing.value: Sampled bound risks use currently filed and approved forms; unfiled forms fail.

checklist.step: Confirm rate filings are approved before use
checklist.value: The rating basis is checked to be an approved filing effective before the risk's effective date.

testing.value: Sampled risks price on approved filings; use of an unapproved rate fails.

answers.value: The identified information/analysis gaps in the referral, for which additional analysis is requested to complete the review; scope is the individual referral's open items.
During senior/chief underwriter review, once gaps are identified and before disposition; requests are issued the same business day.
Each request specifies the gap, the analysis needed, the assignee, and the due date; a request without an assignee or due date is not issued.
The count of identified gaps equals the count of analysis requests issued; open requests reconcile to those returned plus pending, with no dropped items.
Requests and their responses are recorded on the referral with author, timestamp, and version; retained 5 years.
Requests not returned by the due date are logged as an exception and escalated; the referral stays open (no disposition) until all gaps are closed.
The requested analysis must be produced on the approved methodology/model version so results are comparable to the case file.
The request states the sensitivity ranges to test (e.g. rate, frequency, limit) so the returned analysis addresses the material drivers.
Materiality thresholds for the gap are stated so the additional analysis focuses on items that could change the decision (>10% of technical price or authority limit).
Monthly sample of 20 referrals that generated additional-analysis requests.
PASS = each identified gap has a clear, assigned, dated request and a recorded response before disposition; FAIL = a gap disposed without the requested analysis.
Overdue or unmet requests escalate to the CUO/Actuarial lead; the referral cannot be disposed until the analysis is received or the gap is formally accepted.
Acceptance = all identified gaps have issued requests and returned analysis sufficient to complete the review.
Evidence resides on the referral record in ALIP with the request log and returned analysis attached.
The additional-analysis request specifies the approved methodology/model version and parameter source required to close the gap; recorded on the referral.

checklist.step: Require the minimum information needed to complete underwriting
checklist.value: Gaps against minimum submission requirements are turned into specific, assigned analysis requests before disposition.

testing.value: Sampled referrals show all minimum-information gaps were requested and closed before disposition; open gaps fail.

checklist.step: Document requests and responses in the file
checklist.value: Each analysis request and its response are recorded on the referral.

testing.value: Sampled referrals contain a complete request-and-response log; missing items fail.
